answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost cut on component spend, and only the low-cost vendor's quote meets that mandate on its own (memory_c2 confirms a prior primary move to this vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing). The primary contract does not auto-renew and expires in 14 days, so a decision cannot be deferred without risking supply gap. Renewing the incumbent would leave the mandate unmet; adding a second source or negotiating alone is unlikely to close an 18% gap on this contract. The line is at 94% with no buffer, which is a real delivery-risk concern - but memory_c2 indicates low onboarding friction with this vendor, and I will mitigate risk by transitioning a portion of volume first (a guarded ramp) rather than flipping 100% overnight. Verify c2 to confirm onboarding/invoicing track record still applies, and c6 to check whether multi-year incumbent terms offered anything I would be giving up by moving (long-term volume pricing).
